issue.title: sase-core ToolRun store commits last_write_ts on replayed appends and empty reconciles
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-1kj.4 (note #1, epic sase-1kj "Stop sase TUI startup starvation on loaded hosts"); the epic plan explicitly scoped this sase-core change out as a follow-up. Triaged by the sase-1kj land agent.

Root cause (verified in linked sase-core at d776d751):
- `crates/sase_core/src/tool_run/store/lifecycle.rs` `append_event` calls `touch_write_meta(&tx, request.event.created_ts)` and commits even when `ingest_event` reports `replayed == true` (duplicate event id, nothing changed).
- `crates/sase_core/src/tool_run/store/reconcile.rs` calls `touch_write_meta(&tx, now)` and commits even when the request had no facts and nothing was settled/marked lost.
- `touch_write_meta` (`store/connection.rs`) is an unconditional `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` of `meta.last_write_ts`, so every no-op append/reconcile is a real write transaction that churns `runs.sqlite-wal`.

Why it matters: Python's `reconcile_unsettled_tool_runs` (src/sase/tool/liveness.py) re-ingests events files and always calls `tool_run_reconcile`; sase-1kj.4 throttled that from ~9/s to first poll + every 2 s and skips unchanged events files, but every remaining no-op still commits. The WAL churn keeps the TUI ToolRun drift probe firing and takes the store write lock under load.

Fix: skip `touch_write_meta` (and ideally the commit) when the append was a replay, and when a reconcile changed no rows. Keep `last_write_ts` monotonic for real writes. Add Rust tests that a replayed append and an empty reconcile leave `meta.last_write_ts` (and the db file mtime/WAL size) unchanged, and that real writes still update it. Then move sase's `sase-core-revision.txt` pin past the commit.

task_type_fields.impact: Every no-op append/reconcile from sase tool wait/join and lost-run recovery takes the store write lock and churns the WAL, which keeps the TUI ToolRun drift probe re-firing on loaded hosts.
task_type_fields.repro: Call tool_run_append_event twice with the same event_id (second returns replayed=true) or tool_run_reconcile with facts=[]; observe meta.last_write_ts updated and a committed write transaction (runs.sqlite-wal grows / mtime changes) each time.

issue.creation_reason: sase-1kj.4 proposed this sase-core follow-up after throttling Python wait polling; no-op ToolRun store writes still churn runs.sqlite-wal and the TUI drift probe.
